# Runner CLI reference

<!-- Generated by scripts/docs/generate_cli_reference.py; edit parser help in xfuser/config/args.py. -->

This page is generated from the runner's argument parser. See the
[runner guide](runner.md) for launch options, examples, model defaults,
and compatibility restrictions. Dedicated model examples use a different parser.

**Parser defaults are not necessarily effective model defaults.** An omitted
value may be resolved by the selected model or configuration validation;
`None` does not by itself mean that a feature is disabled. A registered
option is not a promise that every model or device supports it.

Runner long options accept underscores or dashes (for example,
`--ulysses_degree` and `--ulysses-degree`). The spellings below are those
registered by argparse, including negative spellings for Boolean options.

In the syntax column, `TEXT`, `INT`, and `FLOAT` name value types; `VALUE`
uses the format described by the option's help.
`CHOICE` refers to the accepted values listed in the description.
Brackets mean optional values:
`[TEXT ...]` accepts zero or more, and `TEXT [TEXT ...]` accepts one or more.
Flags without a value placeholder take no value. Boolean positive spellings
enable a setting and their `--no-...` spellings disable it.

## Model selection and adapters

| Syntax | Parser default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| <a id="-model"></a><a id="--model"></a>`--model` `TEXT` | `None` | **Required.** Registered model alias or Hugging Face repository ID. Local checkpoint loading is model-specific. |
| <a id="-lora_path"></a><a id="--lora_path"></a>`--lora_path` `VALUE` | `None` | LoRA repository or local path to fuse at startup (supported runners only). |
| <a id="-lora_weight_name"></a><a id="--lora_weight_name"></a>`--lora_weight_name` `VALUE` | `None` | LoRA weight filename within --lora\_path when it names a repository or directory. |
| <a id="-lora_scale"></a><a id="--lora_scale"></a>`--lora_scale` `FLOAT` | `1.0` | Finite scale applied when fusing a startup LoRA adapter. |
| <a id="-vdn_transformer_dir"></a><a id="--vdn_transformer_dir"></a>`--vdn_transformer_dir` `VALUE` | `None` | Path to the materialized VDN-H3 transformer directory (must contain a transformer/ subfolder). Overrides the VDN\_H3\_TRANSFORMER\_DIR environment variable. Required when --model is OpenVDN/vdn-minimax-h3 (or VDN-H3). |
| <a id="-vdn_window_backend"></a><a id="--vdn_window_backend"></a>`--vdn_window_backend` `{sdpa,aiter,aiter_ck,aiter_fp8}` | `None` | VDN-H3 only: override the window-softmax varlen kernel. By default it is derived from --attention\_backend (SDPA-&gt;sdpa, AITER-&gt;aiter\_ck, AITER\_FP8-&gt;aiter\_fp8); 'aiter' selects AITER's Triton varlen bf16 kernel. |
| <a id="-task"></a><a id="--task"></a>`--task` `TEXT` | `None` | Task to perform. Only applicable if the model supports multiple tasks. |
| <a id="-distilled_transformer_path"></a><a id="--distilled_transformer_path"></a>`--distilled_transformer_path` `VALUE` | `None` | Path to the high-noise distilled transformer safetensors file. |
| <a id="-distilled_transformer_2_path"></a><a id="--distilled_transformer_2_path"></a>`--distilled_transformer_2_path` `VALUE` | `None` | Path to the low-noise distilled transformer\_2 safetensors file. |

## Loading and CPU offload

| Syntax | Parser default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| <a id="-memory_efficient_sharding"></a><a id="--memory_efficient_sharding"></a>`--memory_efficient_sharding` | `False` | Reduce peak VRAM during load: shard transformer blocks one at a time on GPU during init, so the full unsharded component never materializes on device. Slightly slower to load - use if the model OOMs on GPU during init. Requires --fully\_shard\_degree &gt; 1. |
| <a id="-memory_efficient_replicated_load"></a><a id="--memory_efficient_replicated_load"></a>`--memory_efficient_replicated_load` | `False` | Reduce replicated-weight host memory on supported multi-rank layouts by loading on rank 0 and broadcasting to peers built on meta. With supported PipeFusion runners, stream only stage-local transformer blocks instead. Conflicts with transformer tensor parallelism and untargeted FSDP; a single-rank run remains eager. |
| <a id="-enable_sequential_cpu_offload"></a><a id="--enable_sequential_cpu_offload"></a>`--enable_sequential_cpu_offload` | `False` | Move weights from CPU as individual submodules execute; saves device memory at a latency cost. |
| <a id="-enable_model_cpu_offload"></a><a id="--enable_model_cpu_offload"></a>`--enable_model_cpu_offload` | `False` | Move whole pipeline components between CPU and device as needed on supported models. |
| <a id="-enable_group_cpu_offload"></a><a id="--enable_group_cpu_offload"></a>`--enable_group_cpu_offload` | `False` | Stream groups of weights from CPU: block-level for compiled components, leaf-level otherwise. |
| <a id="-group_offload_low_cpu_mem"></a><a id="--group_offload_low_cpu_mem"></a>`--group_offload_low_cpu_mem` | `False` | With --enable\_group\_cpu\_offload, pin tensors on demand instead of pre-pinning whole components. Reduces pinned host memory at a possible latency cost. |

Requires --enable\_tiling. Must be used with --vae\_tile\_overlap\_width. Height and width may differ; use 0 for an inactive strip axis. |

## Attention backends and communication

| Syntax | Parser default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| <a id="-attention_backend"></a><a id="--attention_backend"></a>`--attention_backend` `TEXT` | `None` | Attention backend name. If omitted, use the model's preferred backend or automatic selection. |
| <a id="-cross_attention_backend"></a><a id="--cross_attention_backend"></a>`--cross_attention_backend` `TEXT` | `None` | Attention backend to use for cross-attention. If not specified, falls back to --attention\_backend. |
| <a id="-mha_v4_kv_splits"></a><a id="--mha_v4_kv_splits"></a>`--mha_v4_kv_splits` `TEXT` | `'1'` | Dense AITER MHA v4 KV split count: 1 disables splitting; 'auto' delegates to AITER. A larger count requires a compatible AITER kernel and shape. Tune with measured latency; splitting adds host overhead and does not apply to every attention format. |
| <a id="-attention_a2a"></a><a id="--attention_a2a"></a>`--attention_a2a` `CHOICE` | `'none'` | AITER Attention A2A input-hop profile. Explicit profiles require and validate a matching --attention\_backend; auto infers the profile from the active backend, including hybrid schedules. When Tier-2 async lowering is unavailable, xDiT uses the Tier-1 ordered path; if neither path is supported, initialization fails and this option must be disabled.<br>Choices: `none`, `auto`, `e4m3-e4m3`, `int8-e4m3`, `mxfp8-e4m3`, `e4m3-mxfp6`, `mxfp6-e4m3`, `mxfp6-mxfp6`, `mxfp4-mxfp4`, `mxfp6-mxfp4`. |
| <a id="-attention_a2a_hadamard"></a><a id="--attention_a2a_hadamard"></a>`--attention_a2a_hadamard` `{auto,preprocess,transport,epilogue,none}` | `'auto'` | Q/K Hadamard placement for Attention A2A. 'auto' uses the recipe default (none for INT8, preprocess for the MX/FP8 profiles). |
| <a id="-ulysses_a2a"></a><a id="--ulysses_a2a"></a>`--ulysses_a2a` `{default,sdma}` | `'default'` | Ulysses all-to-all transport: default (the process group's collective, NCCL or RCCL) or sdma (the GPUs' SDMA copy engines; ROCm, one node). |
| <a id="-ulysses_sdma_head_groups"></a><a id="--ulysses_sdma_head_groups"></a>`--ulysses_sdma_head_groups` `INT` | `None` | With --ulysses\_a2a sdma: split each rank's heads into this many groups (default 2); a group attends while later groups' data is still moving, and its output goes back while later groups attend. |
| <a id="-ulysses_sdma_group_streams"></a><a id="--ulysses_sdma_group_streams"></a>`--ulysses_sdma_group_streams` | `False` | With --ulysses\_a2a sdma: attend each head group on a stream of its own. |
| <a id="-ulysses_sdma_overlap_qkv"></a><a id="--ulysses_sdma_overlap_qkv"></a>`--ulysses_sdma_overlap_qkv` | `False` | With --ulysses\_a2a sdma: overlap the Q/K/V projection with the exchange, in models that support it. Where the QK norm works per head (MiniMax-H3, FLUX.3), Q/K/V are projected one head group at a time, from a second copy of the Q/K/V weights; where it spans all heads (Wan), Q/K are sent before V is projected, in one head group. Under CPU offload only the latter applies. |
| <a id="-use_fp8_comms"></a><a id="--use_fp8_comms"></a>`--use_fp8_comms` | `False` | Quantize Ulysses all-to-all communication to FP8. |
| <a id="-fp8_comms_scale"></a><a id="--fp8_comms_scale"></a>`--fp8_comms_scale` `FLOAT` | `None` | Override the model-specific FP8 communication scale. |
| <a id="-fp8_comms_safety_factor"></a><a id="--fp8_comms_safety_factor"></a>`--fp8_comms_safety_factor` `FLOAT` | `0.85` | Safety factor for the calibrated FP8 comms scale: scale = amax / (FP8\_MAX \* safety\_factor). LOWER it (e.g. 0.4) to enlarge the scale and leave more headroom before fp8 saturation. Default 0.85. |
| <a id="-use_hybrid_attn_schedule"></a><a id="--use_hybrid_attn_schedule"></a>`--use_hybrid_attn_schedule` | `False` | Switch attention backends during denoising on supported models. Performance and quality depend on the schedule. |
| <a id="-hybrid_attn_low_precision_backend"></a><a id="--hybrid_attn_low_precision_backend"></a>`--hybrid_attn_low_precision_backend` `VALUE` | `None` | Low-precision attention backend for hybrid schedule. If set, high-precision backend must also be set. |
| <a id="-hybrid_attn_high_precision_backend"></a><a id="--hybrid_attn_high_precision_backend"></a>`--hybrid_attn_high_precision_backend` `VALUE` | `None` | High-precision attention backend for hybrid schedule. If set, low-precision backend must also be set. |
| <a id="-num_hybrid_attn_high_precision_steps"></a><a id="--num_hybrid_attn_high_precision_steps"></a>`--num_hybrid_attn_high_precision_steps` `INT` | `None` | High-precision denoising steps at both the start and end of the hybrid attention schedule. |
| <a id="-hybrid_attn_schedule"></a><a id="--hybrid_attn_schedule"></a>`--hybrid_attn_schedule` `TEXT` | `None` | Comma-separated per-step attention backend names. Alternative to the low/high-precision backend pair. |

| <a id="-vsa_drop_rates"></a><a id="--vsa_drop_rates"></a>`--vsa_drop_rates` `FLOAT [FLOAT ...]` | `None` | Enable Jenga's per-step sparse schedule. One value applies to all steps; two values switch after the midpoint. Drop rates &lt;=0.25 use dense AITER attention. |

| <a id="-bsa_sparsity"></a><a id="--bsa_sparsity"></a>`--bsa_sparsity` `FLOAT` | `0.75` | TRITON\_BSA: fraction of key blocks each query block skips (top-k). |
| <a id="-bsa_cdf_threshold"></a><a id="--bsa_cdf_threshold"></a>`--bsa_cdf_threshold` `FLOAT` | `0.2` | TRITON\_BSA: also keep the key blocks holding this much attention weight (top-p); 0 disables. |
| <a id="-vsa_reorder_sequence"></a><a id="--vsa_reorder_sequence"></a>`--vsa_reorder_sequence`<br>`--no-vsa_reorder_sequence` | `True` | Reorder Wan video tokens with the sliced Gilbert curve before VSA. |
| <a id="-use_vsa_static_block_mask"></a><a id="--use_vsa_static_block_mask"></a>`--use_vsa_static_block_mask`<br>`--no-use_vsa_static_block_mask` | `True` | Union Gilbert physical-neighbor blocks into the dynamic VSA mask. |
| <a id="-use_vsa_first_frame_mask"></a><a id="--use_vsa_first_frame_mask"></a>`--use_vsa_first_frame_mask`<br>`--no-use_vsa_first_frame_mask` | `True` | Preserve first-frame block relations in the VSA mask. |
| <a id="-vsa_collect_density"></a><a id="--vsa_collect_density"></a>`--vsa_collect_density` | `False` | Record the selected VSA block density for profiling. |

## Step caching

| Syntax | Parser default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| <a id="-use_teacache"></a><a id="--use_teacache"></a>`--use_teacache` | `False` | \[Deprecated\] Use --cache\_method teacache instead. |
| <a id="-use_fbcache"></a><a id="--use_fbcache"></a>`--use_fbcache` | `False` | \[Deprecated\] Use --cache\_method fbcache instead. |
| <a id="-cache_method"></a><a id="--cache_method"></a>`--cache_method` `{teacache,fbcache,dbcache,pipefusion}` | `None` | Step cache for supported models. pipefusion requires pipeline parallelism; other methods reject it. |
| <a id="-cache_config"></a><a id="--cache_config"></a>`--cache_config` `TEXT` | `None` | JSON string of advanced config overrides merged on top of preset defaults. E.g. '{"residual\_diff\_threshold": 0.5, "max\_warmup\_steps": 6}'. Cache-DiT engines use DBCacheConfig fields; in-tree TeaCache/FBCache accept only residual\_diff\_threshold. |

## Benchmarking, profiling, and output

| Syntax | Parser default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| <a id="-num_iterations"></a><a id="--num_iterations"></a>`--num_iterations` `INT` | `1` | Number of iterations to run the model. |
| <a id="-determinism_check"></a><a id="--determinism_check"></a>`--determinism_check` `INT` | `0` | Set to a positive failure threshold to compare every timed iteration with the first using exact equality, not a tolerance. The failure handler is called for each rank enabled by --determinism\_check\_report\_ranks on each divergence until the threshold is reached. Disabled at 0 or below. Enabling retains and compares full output payloads, which adds memory, synchronization, and transfer overhead. |
| <a id="-determinism_check_report_ranks"></a><a id="--determinism_check_report_ranks"></a>`--determinism_check_report_ranks` `TEXT` | `'last'` | Ranks on which determinism failures save serialized outputs. Accepts a comma-separated list of integers, an empty value, or one of: all, first, last, none. Empty and none select no ranks. Defaults to last. Many failures may produce many large output files; restrict output to selected ranks based on model specifics. The none value is useful with a positive --determinism\_check when only log messages, but no files, are needed. |
| <a id="-profile"></a><a id="--profile"></a>`--profile` | `False` | Whether to run Pytorch profiler. See --profile\_wait, --profile\_warmup and --profile\_active for profiler specific warmup. |
| <a id="-profile_wait"></a><a id="--profile_wait"></a>`--profile_wait` `INT` | `2` | wait argument for torch.profiler.schedule. Only used with --profile. |
| <a id="-profile_warmup"></a><a id="--profile_warmup"></a>`--profile_warmup` `INT` | `2` | warmup argument for torch.profiler.schedule. Only used with --profile. |
| <a id="-profile_active"></a><a id="--profile_active"></a>`--profile_active` `INT` | `1` | active argument for torch.profiler.schedule. Only used with --profile. |
| <a id="-profile_capture_phase"></a><a id="--profile_capture_phase"></a>`--profile_capture_phase` | `False` | Profile the CUDA graph recording phase and save the capture trace. |
| <a id="-profile_with_stack"></a><a id="--profile_with_stack"></a>`--profile_with_stack` | `False` | Record call stack info in the profiler. Only used with --profile. |
| <a id="-warmup_calls"></a><a id="--warmup_calls"></a>`--warmup_calls` `INT` | `0` | Full untimed pipeline calls before measured iterations; separate from PipeFusion --warmup\_steps. |
| <a id="-output_directory"></a><a id="--output_directory"></a>`--output_directory` `TEXT` | `'.'` | Directory where to save outputs, profiles and timings. |
